note: Acrostic of trust/guidance/forgiveness: lift-soul, trust, wait, know-ways, penitence, humble-led, keep-covenant, pardon, fear-instructed, friendship, affliction, heart-troubles, integrity, refuge

275947.gloss: lift up my soul to you

dims.v: lift up my soul to you
the self lifts up its soul to God - the whole inner self raised toward him as the psalm opens
v1: 'To you, O LORD, I LIFT UP my SOUL' - the operation raises the entire interior toward God; the acrostic begins by handing the self over.
the self trusts God and pleads not to be put to shame, not to let enemies exult - reliance under threat
v2: 'O my God, in you I TRUST; let me not be put to SHAME' - the operation rests the self on God while the danger of humiliation presses; trust and vulnerability held together.
none who wait for God shall be put to shame, but the wantonly treacherous will - waiting as the vindicated posture
v3: 'none who WAIT for you shall be put to shame' - the operation generalises the trust into patient waiting; the interior that waits is promised it will not be disappointed.
the self asks to be shown God's ways and taught his paths - a desire to be led rightly
v4: 'Make me to KNOW your WAYS, O LORD; teach me your paths' - the operation is a longing to be taught; the interior wants direction, not just rescue.

276069.gloss: for you I wait all day

dims.v: for you I wait all day
the self waits for God all the day long, asking to be led in his truth - sustained, whole-day hope
v5: 'Lead me in your truth and teach me... for you I WAIT all the day long' - distinct from v3: this is the personal, unremitting waiting that fills the whole day.
the self asks God not to remember the sins of its youth but to remember it by steadfast love - penitent appeal for forgetting

v7: 'REMEMBER NOT the SINS of my youth or my transgressions; according to your steadfast love remember me' - the operation is a penitent's plea: let the record of old sin be blotted, and let love be the lens instead.
God leads the humble in what is right and teaches them his way - lowliness as the teachable condition
v9: 'He LEADS the HUMBLE in what is right, and teaches the humble his way' - the operation names the interior God can guide: only the humble are teachable, and they are led.
all God's paths are steadfast love and faithfulness for those who keep his covenant - fidelity that walks in love

v10: 'All the paths of the LORD are steadfast love and faithfulness, for those who KEEP his COVENANT and his testimonies' - the operation is the kept covenant; the interior that holds to God's terms finds all his ways to be love.

275962.gloss: pardon my guilt, for it is great

dims.v: pardon my guilt, for it is great
the self asks pardon for its guilt, honestly owning that it is great - confession without minimising
v11: 'For your name's sake, O LORD, PARDON my GUILT, for it is GREAT' - the operation is unflinching confession: the interior does not shrink the sin but names it great and appeals to God's name.
the one who fears the LORD
whoever fears the LORD, God will instruct in the way he should choose - reverence rewarded with guidance

v12: 'Who is the man who FEARS the LORD? Him will he INSTRUCT in the way that he should choose' - the operation ties instruction to fear: the reverent interior is the one God teaches which way to take.
the God-fearer's soul abides in well-being and his offspring inherit the land - the interior at ease as the fruit of fear
v13: 'His SOUL shall abide in WELL-BEING, and his offspring shall inherit the land' - the operation is rest: the fearing interior settles into a lasting good.
the intimate friendship/counsel of the LORD is for those who fear him, to whom he makes known his covenant - a shared secret

v14: 'The FRIENDSHIP of the LORD is for those who FEAR him, and he makes KNOWN to them his covenant' - the operation is intimacy: the God-fearing interior is admitted to God's confidence, told his secret.
the self asks God to turn and be gracious, for it is lonely and afflicted - the ache of isolation brought to God
v16: 'Turn to me and be GRACIOUS to me, for I am LONELY and AFFLICTED' - the operation names a specific inner condition, solitude joined to affliction, and lays it before God for mercy.

276003.gloss: the troubles of my heart enlarged

dims.v: the troubles of my heart enlarged
the troubles of the self's heart are enlarged; it asks to be brought out of its distresses - inner pressure mounting
v17: 'The TROUBLES of my HEART are ENLARGED; bring me out of my distresses' - the operation registers a swelling of interior anguish, the heart's troubles growing rather than easing.
the self asks that integrity and uprightness preserve it, for it waits on God - character offered as its guard
v21: 'May INTEGRITY and UPRIGHTNESS preserve me, for I WAIT for you' - the operation offers the self's own integrity, held in dependence on God, as the thing that keeps it.
the self asks God to guard and deliver its soul, not letting it be shamed, for it takes refuge in him - shelter as the ground of the plea
v20: 'Oh, GUARD my soul, and deliver me! Let me not be put to shame, for I TAKE REFUGE in you' - the operation shelters the whole self in God; refuge is the reason the plea expects to be answered.
v5: 'LEAD me in your truth and teach me' - the guiding act the desire-to-know asks for.
v5: 'and TEACH me' - the instruction sought.
v6: 'REMEMBER your mercy, O LORD, and your steadfast love' - the love the penitent asks God to recall instead of sin.
v8: 'Good and upright is the LORD; therefore he INSTRUCTS sinners in the way' - God's guiding character behind the leading of the humble.
v18: 'Consider my affliction... and FORGIVE all my sins' - the pardon the confession seeks.
v18: 'CONSIDER my affliction and my trouble' - the divine regard the lonely self pleads for.
v20: 'DELIVER me' - the rescue the refuge-taking expects.
v22: 'REDEEM Israel, O God, out of all his troubles' - the corporate deliverance the psalm closes on.
